hints: Look at the column headings n, $\mu$ and p in that order and check the powers $10^{-6}$, $10^{-9}$ and $10^{-12}$ against each prefix separately.
Remember micro means one-millionth, so $1 \, \mu\text{m} = 10^{-6} \, \text{m}$, which fixes the $\mu$ column to $10^{-6}$.
Remember nano is a thousand times smaller than micro and pico is a thousand times smaller than nano, so use $10^{-6}$ to step down to $10^{-9}$ and then to $10^{-12}$.
walkthrough: Identify what the table needs: the multiplier for nano (n), for micro ($\mu$) and for pico (p) using the powers $10^{-6}$, $10^{-9}$ and $10^{-12}$.
State the SI prefix rule: micro is $10^{-6}$, nano is $10^{-9}$ and pico is $10^{-12}$, each step down by a factor of $10^{-3}$ or 1000.
Check nano: $1 \, \text{nm} = 10^{-9} \, \text{m}$, so the n column must be $10^{-9}$.
Check micro: $1 \, \mu\text{m} = 10^{-6} \, \text{m}$, so the $\mu$ column must be $10^{-6}$, which is 1000 times larger than nano.
Check pico: $1 \, \text{pF} = 10^{-12} \, \text{F}$, so the p column must be $10^{-12}$, which is 1000 times smaller than nano.
The only row with $10^{-9}$ for n, $10^{-6}$ for $\mu$ and $10^{-12}$ for p matches the rule. This is option C.

options.A: It swaps nano and micro, since nano is $10^{-9}$ not $10^{-6}$ and micro is $10^{-6}$ not $10^{-9}$.
options.B: It gives micro as $10^{-12}$ and pico as $10^{-9}$, which reverses their order since micro is larger than pico.
options.C: It correctly gives nano as $10^{-9}$, micro as $10^{-6}$ and pico as $10^{-12}$.
options.D: It reverses the size order, giving nano the smallest value $10^{-12}$ and pico the largest value $10^{-6}$.
